meta.scope: Yemen Batch 6 — International partners densification: Saudi support, major trade partners (China, Saudi, India, Turkey), and external architecture framing under severe conflict constraints.

candidates.title: Saudi Arabia economic and grant support framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from Saudi Program and bilateral sources
candidates.description: Framing of Saudi Arabia as the principal external economic and fiscal supporter of the internationally recognized government. Grants, central-bank deposits, salary support and development projects form a critical residual financing channel under collapsed oil revenue.
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality bilateral external-financing node for the IRG side.

candidates.title: Major merchandise trade partners statistics
candidates.description: Statistics on major trade partners. China, Saudi Arabia, India, Turkey and Brazil are leading import origins (food, fuel, consumer and intermediate goods); India and Saudi Arabia feature among top export destinations for residual non-oil goods. The trade deficit is large and structural.
candidates.notes: Core formal trade-partner densification under constrained volumes.

candidates.title: Yemen external economic and humanitarian architecture framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from UN, bilateral and monitoring sources
candidates.description: System-level framing of Yemen’s external architecture: Saudi and other bilateral grants, UN humanitarian system, limited formal trade, and residual diplomatic/economic engagement under conflict and dual authority. Continuously cited in every macro and humanitarian assessment.

candidates.title: Yemen international densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from bilateral and trade sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding Saudi economic/grant support, major trade partners, and external economic/humanitarian architecture into a coherent international layer under severe conflict constraints.
